chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the urine of donkeys and mules. He said: “Wash your garment.” He said: I said, “Then what about their droppings?” He said: “That is greater than that.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All of these reports are to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah (dislike). What indicates that is what we have presented in our major book, and also what has preceded in this book: that regarding that whose flesh may be eaten, there is no harm in its urine and dung. Since these things are not among those forbidden in flesh, their urine and droppings would not be forbidden. This is also indicated by that.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: the urines; referring to the urine of animals under legal discussion
key_terms.اغْسِلْ: wash; an instruction to cleanse the garment
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike or reprehensibility short of prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility or absence of legal objection

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the urine and droppings of donkeys and mules in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling concerning the urine and droppings of donkeys and mules, where the apparent wording instructs washing the garment. Shaykh al-Tusi then explains that such reports are carried upon karahah rather than prohibition, reconciling them with other narrations on animal excretions and legal purity.
